facts: The golden crown for today's school play, The Dragon's Birthday, has gone missing from the hall.
Mrs. Abara left the crown on its cushion on the stage steps at ten past twelve.
At a quarter to one the cushion was empty.
Nina plays the queen, and she was heard wishing the play would be cancelled.
Everyone is now whispering about Nina.

timeline: Wednesday 12:00: lunch begins. Nina, sick with nerves about her big speech, heads for the bike shed in the playground to practise it alone. She asks her friend Sam to say she spent lunch with him in the library, so nobody finds out and laughs. Sam signs in at the library at 12:05, alone.
12:00 to 12:45: Mr. Pike is up a ladder on the bike-shed roof, mending the felt. From there he can see the art room windows across the way, and from about 12:06 Nina beside the shed, the whole time.
12:05: Mrs. Abara, still in the hall, sees Nina hurry past the hall door towards the playground with a bundle of script cards stuffed under her jumper. Nina reaches the bike shed a minute later.
12:10: Mrs. Abara sets the golden crown on its cushion on the stage steps and goes to the staff room for tea.

12:12: Leo comes into the hall to fetch the gold glitter paint. He sits on the stage steps to tie his shoe and squashes the crown flat, smearing gold glitter over the step and the seat of his trousers. He panics.

12:15: Leo wraps the bent crown in his painting apron, hurries to the art room and wedges it behind the big paper dragon. He tries to glue the bend flat, and leaves the glue tube without its lid. Mr. Pike sees him through the window. Leo decides to say nothing and to point at Nina, who has been grumbling about the play.
12:45: Mrs. Abara comes back and finds only the squashed cushion. The play starts at two.
truth.motive: Leo never meant to break the crown: he sat on it by accident. He hid it and blamed Nina, who had been grumbling about the play, because he was terrified of getting into trouble.

hall.name: The School Hall
facts: The hall is big and echoing, and it smells of floor polish.
A stage with wooden steps stands at one end.
A props table and a rail of dragon costumes stand beside the stage.

art_room.name: The Art Room
facts: Paint pots, brushes and glittery scraps cover every table.
Half-finished scenery leans against the walls.
The sink drips into a stained bucket.

library.name: The Library
facts: The library is hushed and smells of old paper and carpet.
A desk by the door holds a stamp, a pencil pot and a clipboard.

spots.name: the sign-in sheet on the desk

playground.name: The Playground
facts: The playground has painted hopscotch squares, a climbing frame and a row of bikes.
A ladder leans on the roof of the bike shed.
A pot of black roofing felt sits beside the ladder.

abara.name: Mrs. Abara
abara.personality: Brisk, kind and a little flustered, with a pencil behind her ear. She runs the school play and wants everyone to feel brave.

demeanor.open: Worried about the two o'clock curtain, but warm and glad of help.

knows.fact: Mrs. Abara runs the school play, The Dragon's Birthday.
The dragon costumes for the play hang on the rail beside the stage.

appearance: Mrs. Abara is a teacher with a pencil tucked behind her ear.
She wears a long cardigan with a rolled-up script in its pocket.

leo.name: Leo
leo.personality: Cheerful, chatty and a bit of a fidget. He loves painting scenery, and when he is scared he talks too fast and looks at his shoes.

demeanor.guarded: Chatty and too keen to help. He keeps steering the talk towards Nina.
demeanor.shaken: Quieter. He has stopped pointing at anyone and answers in short bursts.
demeanor.cornered: Out of excuses. His eyes fill up and he chews his sleeve.
demeanor.cleared: Tearful but relieved. He wants everyone to know it was an accident.

knows.fact: Leo paints the scenery for the school play.

appearance: Leo is a boy with messy hair and paint on his fingers.
He wears a school jumper with paint-spattered sleeves.

nina.name: Nina
nina.personality: Clever and quiet, with a very good memory for lines and a very bad case of stage fright. Prickly when she feels cornered, and fiercely loyal to Sam.

demeanor.open: Defensive and jumpy. She knows people are whispering about her.
demeanor.cleared: Relieved and a little embarrassed. She is ready to be brave.

knows.fact: Nina plays the queen in The Dragon's Birthday and knows all her lines by heart.

appearance: Nina is a girl with her hair in two tight plaits.
She wears her school jumper with the sleeves pulled over her hands.

sam.name: Sam
sam.personality: Gentle, loyal and bad at lying. He would rather read a comic than argue with anybody.

demeanor.open: Easy and friendly, glad of company.
demeanor.guarded: Nervous. He holds his comic up high and answers a beat too fast.
demeanor.cleared: Sorry and relieved. He is glad to stop pretending.

knows.fact: The library has a comic corner with beanbags.

appearance: Sam is a boy with round glasses.
He carries a comic everywhere he goes.

pike.name: Mr. Pike
pike.personality: Slow, dry and observant. He sees everything from his ladder and only speaks when somebody asks.

demeanor.open: Easygoing and helpful. He answers exactly what he is asked, no more.

knows.fact: Mr. Pike is the school caretaker and mends whatever breaks.

appearance: Mr. Pike is a tall, thin man in blue overalls.
He wears a tool belt and a flat cap.

clue_gold_on_steps.fact: Gold glitter is smeared across the middle stage step. The velvet cushion lies on the step with a big bottom-shaped dent in it. Someone sat down right here, on something that is now gone.

clue_glue_out.fact: The tube of super-strong glue on the paint shelf has no lid, and sticky gold glitter fingerprints are on it. Someone has been gluing something gold.

clue_crown_behind_dragon.fact: The golden crown is wedged behind the big paper dragon. It is bent flat in the middle, with a line of glue squeezed along the bend. Someone tried to mend it and hid it.

clue_signin_sheet.fact: The library's lunchtime sign-in sheet has one name: 'Sam, 12:05'. No second name is beside it, and Nina's name is nowhere on the page.

source.spot: the sign-in sheet on the desk

clue_script_cards.fact: A pile of script cards lies behind the bike shed, crossed out and rewritten, with 'SPEAK UP!' scribbled on top in Nina's writing. The grass there is trampled flat, as if somebody stood on that spot for ages.

abara_missing.fact: Mrs. Abara says the golden crown is gone. She put it on its cushion on the stage steps at ten past twelve and went to the staff room. When she came back at a quarter to one, only the cushion was there.

abara_nina_jumper.fact: Mrs. Abara says that just after twelve, before she put the crown down, she saw Nina hurry past the hall door with something bulging under her jumper.

abara_nina_wish.fact: Mrs. Abara says Nina told her last week that she hoped something would happen so there would be no play. Mrs. Abara thought it was just nerves, but now she does not know what to think.

leo_alibi.fact: Leo says he was in the art room all lunchtime, painting the dragon's wing, and never went near the hall.
leo_alibi.why: He is terrified of getting into trouble for squashing the crown.

react_leo_seat.fact: Leo keeps tugging his jumper down over the back of his trousers, where something gold sparkles.

leo_blames_nina.fact: Leo says it was Nina: she said she wished the play would be cancelled, and he saw her sneaking about with a bundle.
leo_blames_nina.why: Pointing at somebody else keeps eyes off him.

leo_drops_nina.fact: Leo says that if Nina was only practising, then maybe it was not Nina. He only thought she looked cross.

leo_admits_hall.fact: Leo admits he did go to the hall to fetch the gold glitter paint, and he sat on the stage steps to tie his shoe.

leo_confession.fact: Leo says he sat on the crown and squashed it flat. He tried to glue it straight and hid it behind the dragon, and he was too scared to tell anyone.

nina_not_me.fact: Nina says she did not take the crown and was not even in the hall, and that the investigator should ask Sam.

react_nina_cards.fact: Nina hides a fistful of crumpled cards behind her back and glances at the bike shed.

nina_admits_practising.fact: Nina says she was behind the bike shed practising her big speech. She gets so nervous that she feels sick. She asked Sam to say she was with him because she did not want anyone to laugh at her.

line.text: They say it is fine to be nervous, or promise not to tell the others.

sam_alibi_nina.fact: Sam says Nina was in the library with him all lunchtime, reading comics, from twelve until the bell, and that she never went anywhere near the hall.
sam_alibi_nina.why: Nina begged him to cover for her, and he is loyal.

react_sam_comic.fact: Sam holds his comic up so high that it hides his face, and the page never turns.

sam_retracts.fact: Sam admits Nina was not with him: he signed in at five past twelve and was on his own all lunchtime. Nina asked him to say she was with him because she was doing something secret, and he does not know what.

pike_roof.fact: Mr. Pike says he has been up on the bike-shed roof since twelve, mending the felt, right across from the art room windows.

clue_pike_saw_bundle.fact: Mr. Pike says that at about a quarter past twelve he saw Leo through the art room window. Leo tucked a bundle wrapped in his apron behind the big paper dragon, and he looked very guilty.

clue_pike_saw_nina.fact: Mr. Pike says that from a few minutes past twelve until a quarter to one, Nina was beside the bike shed, whispering to herself. He could see her the whole time, and she never went near the hall.

nina_alibi_early.text: Nina was in the library with Sam all lunchtime, so she cannot have taken the crown.

nina_cleared.text: Nina is cleared: she was behind the bike shed practising, in Mr. Pike's sight, the whole time the crown was being squashed.

bundle_explained.text: The bundle under Nina's jumper was her script cards, and her wish for no play was stage fright.
bundle_explained.resolves: red herring: Nina's bundle and her wish

culprit_leo.text: Leo squashed the crown by accident and hid it, then pointed at Nina.

how.text: The crown was squashed when Leo sat on it by mistake; nobody meant to break it.
